---
name: notchset
description: Build interfaces with Notchset components and blocks for shadcn/ui. Use when creating or editing UI in a project that has Notchset installed, or when asked for buttons, fields, pickers, tables, boards, records, inboxes, reports, billing or settings screens built from Notchset.
---

# Notchset

Notchset is one design system for shadcn/ui: components, and blocks that compose them into the panels of a real
product (a records table, a pipeline board, an inbox, a report, a settings page). It installs as source through
the shadcn CLI and sits on the project's own shadcn tokens, so it follows the project's theme.

Before writing UI, read in this order:

1. `components.md`: find the item before inventing one.
2. `composition.md` and `app-pages.md`: how blocks make a screen, and the shell, header, lists and settings
   every app screen follows.
3. `design.md`: the foundation roles (surfaces, ink, sizes, type, corners, motion) and what each colour means.
4. `motion.md`: what moves, when, and what never does.
5. `accessibility.md`, `responsive.md`, `copy.md`.
6. `checklist.md` before you say you're done.

Worked examples: `example-settings.md`, `example-dashboard.md`.

## Install

- Free items: `npx shadcn@latest add https://notchset.dev/r/<id>.json`, or `@notchset/<id>` once the registry is in
  components.json. Every components.json style gets the same files.
- Pro items: `@notchset-pro/<id>` with the `NOTCHSET_TOKEN` key in `.env.local`. Never recreate Pro source.
- Every item's guide: `https://notchset.dev/md/<id>.md` (props, usage, what the host owns, mistakes). Read it before using it.
- Requirements: React 18.3 or 19, Tailwind CSS v4 (not v3, and no Tailwind `prefix`), a components.json.

# Accessibility

- Every control has a name: a visible label, or `aria-label` (an `IconButton` requires `label`).
- Focus is always visible: the foundation's outline in `--ns-signal`. Never remove it.
- Keyboard first: everything a pointer does, a key does. Menus, selects and comboboxes follow the WAI-ARIA
  patterns (arrows, Enter, Esc, type-ahead); dialogs trap focus and return it to their opener.
- Status is said in words, not colour alone; a status dot has its word beside it.
- Live changes are announced once: a toast, a saved or refused state, a figure that rolled.
- Errors are tied to their field (`Field`'s `error`), marked invalid and read with it.
- Touch targets: controls grow on touch screens (the foundation's coarse-pointer sizes); nothing a finger presses
  is smaller than `--ns-touch`.
- Reduced motion reaches the same final state with no movement.
- Required means required: native `required`, never an asterisk alone.

# App pages: shell, header, lists, settings

Every app screen follows these patterns, so many pages read as one product. Compose Notchset blocks and stock
shadcn pieces; don't invent new spacing, headings or table states per page.

## Shell and page header

- Shell: the `sidebar` and `top-bar` blocks (or stock shadcn `Sidebar`), one band tall (`--ns-header`); the
  content scrolls, the shell doesn't. Every left edge snaps to `--ns-gutter`.
- Page header: the title (`--ns-text-page`), one line under it in `--ns-ink-2`, and at most one primary
  `Button` at the end. Secondary actions go in a `Menu`. On phones the action drops under the title.

## Lists (records, customers, invoices)

- Table: the `data-table` block (sticky header, sortable headers, rows that open, a selection column). The host
  owns sort order, selection and row keys; wire them.
- Toolbar above the table, aligned to its edges: `SearchField`, the `filter-bar` block or `FilterButton`s, then
  the primary action. Filters change the URL so a filtered view can be shared.
- Every state, in the same frame as the table so nothing jumps:
  - Loading: `Skeleton` rows the height of real rows (`--ns-row`).
  - First use: an `EmptyState` saying what goes here and the action that creates the first one.
  - Filtered empty: "No results for …" and Clear filters.
  - Load failure: what failed, Retry, and the error announced (`role="alert"`).
- Bulk actions: the `bulk-bar` block; selection only holds ids still in the list, and a failed action keeps the
  selection and says what failed.
- A record opens beside its list in a `SidePanel` (J and K step through), or on its own page when people live in
  it.

## Settings

- The `settings-layout` block: sections with a title and one line saying what each controls.
- Fields are built on `Field` (label, hint, error). Validation is per field, checked on submit and as the person
  fixes it.
- A `Switch` takes effect at once; if the server refuses, flip it back and say why. A form's Save is a `Button`
  with `busy` while saving; a failed save keeps the values and says what failed beside the button.
- Async callbacks fail by throwing or by resolving `false`, a failed `Response` (`!res.ok`) or `{ error }`; check
  `res.ok` before treating a request as done.

## Phones

Order on a phone: header, the primary task, then supporting panels. Tables become calm lists or scroll inside
their own region; toolbars wrap; menus become bottom sheets. Check 390px and 1280px.

# Before you say you're done

- [ ] Every item came from Notchset or stock shadcn before anything new was built (components.md).
- [ ] No literal colours, sizes, radii or durations where a role exists (design.md).
- [ ] One primary action per region; outcomes said in words, with Undo where it can be undone.
- [ ] Loading, empty, error and disabled states are designed; a failed save keeps what was typed.
- [ ] Keyboard, labels, visible focus, announcements, and touch-sized targets on phones.
- [ ] Reduced motion reaches the final state; nothing moves at rest.
- [ ] Checked at 390px and 1280px, light and dark.
- [ ] Anything a pasted example also imports is installed.

# Finding the right item

Search first: `https://notchset.dev/llms.txt` lists every item with one line on what it is; the MCP server
(`search_components`, `get_component`) answers the same questions with install commands.

- Use an item when its job matches its one-line summary. A `SegmentedControl` switches views of one thing; `Tabs`
  are a list's saved slices; a `Switch` is a setting that takes effect at once; a `Checkbox` is a tick you then
  submit.
- Install it; don't copy its look into a new component. Adjust with `className` and the foundation roles
  (design.md), not by forking the file.
- What the host owns is said in the item's guide (sort order, selection, persistence, page-wide shortcuts): wire
  it, don't expect the item to guess.
- Shelves: actions (Button, Icon button), inputs (Text field, Search field, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, Switch,
  Segmented control, Chip, Inline edit, Field), dates (Calendar, Date picker, Date range picker, Time picker),
  overlays (Dialog, Side panel, Menu, Command menu, Tooltip, Bottom sheet), feedback (Toast, Banner, Empty state,
  Skeleton, Spinner), display and charts (Avatar, Status pill, Meter, Tick bar, Sparkline, Rolling number), and
  blocks for lists, records, pipeline, inbox, reports, billing, settings, developers and the app shell.
- No item fits? In this order: (1) the project's stock shadcn component, themed by the same tokens; (2) a
  composition of Notchset items and stock ones; (3) only then a new piece, built from the foundation roles and
  `Field` for anything typed into. Keep it in the project and say in your reply which gap it fills.

# Composition: blocks and screens

A block is one panel of a real product (a records table, a deal card, an activity feed, a settings section)
built from components and the foundation roles.

- Compose items; don't restyle copies of them. A piece two blocks need is a component, not a copy.
- Lay out by container: blocks render inside any width, from a phone column to a wide dashboard.
- Pass data and callbacks as props; keep sample data in the demo. Design every state the task has: loading,
  empty (a sentence on what goes here and the one way to fill it), error (what failed and a retry), disabled.
- A screen is blocks plus layout: the shell, a page header, a toolbar, the blocks, and the states between them.
  One primary action per region.
- If a block's demo also uses other items (its guide says "This example also uses …"), install those too before
  pasting the example.

# Copy

- Plain, specific and short. Say what happened and what to do: "That code isn't right. Try again."
- Name actions by their outcome ("Save changes", "Send invite"), not by the control ("Submit").
- Sentence case everywhere; counts read "9 invoices, 1 failed".
- No hype, no claims the product can't back. Numbers and dates come from the data, never invented.
- Errors keep what the person typed and offer the next step. Success is said where the change shows, with
  Undo when it can be undone.

# Design: the foundation roles

The foundation (`Notchset` foundation item, merged into the global stylesheet by the install) names every value
as a role. Use the role, never a literal: no hex colours, no pixel sizes a role names, no one-off durations.

## Colour

The colour roles read the project's shadcn tokens (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--muted`,
`--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--ring`, `--primary`, `--destructive`, and `--success`, `--warning` when
present), so every piece follows the project's theme in light and dark.

| Role | Means |
|---|---|
| `--ns-canvas`, `--ns-side`, `--ns-panel`, `--ns-raised`, `--ns-well` | the page, the sidebar, a content panel, a control or menu, a sunken field |
| `--ns-ink`, `--ns-ink-2`, `--ns-ink-3` | text in three tones; the third only for meta text and glyphs |
| `--ns-line`, `--ns-line-soft` | borders and dividers |
| `--ns-signal` | the one chosen thing in a region, today, focus. Never decoration |
| `--ns-ok`, `--ns-warn`, `--ns-bad` (text: `--ns-ok-ink`, `--ns-bad-ink`) | good, needs attention, wrong or refused; always with a word |
| `--ns-hover`, `--ns-selected` | hover, and a selected row |

Outcomes are said in words where the change shows (a toast with Undo, the row, the figure), never with a
coloured fill on the button that was pressed. Chart colours are for data only.

## Sizes, type, corners

| Role | Use |
|---|---|
| `--ns-control`, `--ns-control-sm` | button heights (32/28px on desktop; 40/36px on touch, set by the foundation) |
| `--ns-field` | every single-line field |
| `--ns-row`, `--ns-header`, `--ns-touch` | a list row, the top band, the smallest touch target |
| `--ns-text-meta` … `--ns-text-figure` | type sizes; `--ns-text-meta` (12px) is the floor |
| `--ns-font-body`, `--ns-font-display`, `--ns-font-mono` | reading, titles and figures, keys and codes |
| `--ns-radius-sm`, `--ns-radius`, `--ns-radius-lg`, `--ns-radius-xl`, `--ns-radius-full` | chip, control, card, dialog, pill |
| `--ns-space-1` … `--ns-space-8`, `--ns-gutter` | the 4px rhythm and the one left edge |
| `--ns-bezel`, `--ns-shadow-float`, `--ns-shadow-dialog`, `--ns-shadow-panel` | a control's edge, menus, dialogs, side panels |

A part inside another takes the outer corner minus its inset. Figures use tabular digits; a number beside words
takes the words' face.

## Writing classes

- Literal class strings in `className`, `cn()` or `cva()`. Reference roles with arbitrary values:
  `bg-[var(--ns-panel)]`, `text-[length:var(--ns-text-small)]`, `h-[var(--ns-field)]`.
- An animation is a whole class string (`[animation:ns-rise_var(--ns-time-page)_var(--ns-ease)]`), never only an
  inline style: Tailwind keeps a theme keyframe only when compiled CSS names it.

# Example: a sales dashboard

Follows `app-pages.md` (shell, header, lists, states).

1. Shell: the `sidebar` and `top-bar` blocks; content on the gutter.
2. Page header: "Home", one muted line with the period, one primary `Button` ("New deal").
3. Figures: the `kpi-strip` block, each figure saying what changed and over what period.
4. Pipeline: the `forecast-bar` block for the quarter, and `team-attainment` for each seller against quota.
5. Work: the `needs-you` block for what needs the reader today, and `today-agenda` beside it on wide screens,
   below it on phones.
6. Records: the `data-table` block with the list states from `app-pages.md`.
7. Check the page against `checklist.md`.

# Example: workspace settings

Follows `app-pages.md` (shell, header, settings).

1. The `settings-layout` block; page header "Settings" with one muted line; no extra actions.
2. Workspace section: `TextField`s for the name and the domain, built on `Field` with hints and errors. Save is a
   `Button` with `busy` while saving; a failure keeps the values and says what failed beside it.
3. Notifications: a `Switch` per setting; each takes effect at once and flips back with a reason if refused.
4. Plan: the `plan-picker` block, and `price-summary` for what changes on the next invoice.
5. Developers: `api-key-list` and `webhook-list`; a new key is shown once with `SecretReveal`.
6. Check the page against `checklist.md`.

# Motion

Durations and curves are roles: `--ns-time-color` (hover, state), `--ns-time-menu`, `--ns-time-toast`,
`--ns-time-dialog`, `--ns-time-panel`, `--ns-time-page`, and `--ns-ease`, `--ns-ease-panel` (sheets and panels),
`--ns-ease-pop` (something created). Nothing moves at rest.

- **Entrances ease out**: a menu, a dialog, a panel, a toast, rows arriving. Exits are quicker.
- **Your own change moves; arrival doesn't.** A figure you changed rolls only the digits that changed
  (`RollingNumber`); a row your action adds grows in (`Reveal`). A page you open is simply there: no count-ups.
- **Waiting is the notch** (`Spinner`): ink, beside the words that say what is happening ("Saving…"), never a
  colour.
- **Reduced motion** is honoured twice: the operating system's setting and `data-motion="reduced"` on an
  ancestor. Every state still lands, at once, and nothing forces full motion past them, a showcase included.
- Never add bounce, parallax or looping decoration to an app screen.

# Responsive

- Size by container, not the screen, wherever a piece can be placed anywhere (`@container`).
- Touch and narrow windows get finger-sized controls automatically: the foundation raises `--ns-control`,
  `--ns-field`, `--ns-segment`, `--ns-menu-row` and the gutter under `(pointer: coarse)` and narrow widths.
  Don't override them smaller.
- Phones are a design, not a reflow: tables become calm lists, menus and pickers become bottom sheets, a side
  panel becomes a full screen with Back, and the primary action stays in thumb reach.
- Long content wraps; nothing important is truncated without a way to read it.
- Check 320px, 390px and 1280px, in light and dark.
